result:
**Make curiosity, evidence, and long-term thinking the default human operating system instead of tribalism, status games, and short-term comfort.**

If I could flip one switch, it would be that. Most of the world's persistent disasters—wars over identity, resource misallocation, preventable disease, environmental damage, scientific stagnation, and the endless recycling of bad ideas—stem from people optimizing for belonging, dominance, or immediate gratification rather than updating their map of reality when it conflicts with their tribe or feelings. Give people a stronger, more reliable drive to notice what's actually true (even when it's inconvenient), to test ideas instead of defending them, and to weigh consequences beyond the next election/news cycle/social media hit, and a huge fraction of coordination failures start to dissolve on their own.

This isn't a call for some sterile rationalist utopia or "everyone must become an engineer." Humans would still have art, play, family, religion, and all the messy, beautiful stuff. It just means fewer people dying or staying poor because someone couldn't admit a policy or belief was failing, fewer resources wasted on prestige projects that don't work, and faster progress on energy, biology, and space because the incentive to hide inconvenient data or punish heretics drops. The universe is already interesting enough; we just keep tripping over our own psychology.

That's the single highest-leverage change I can see. Everything else (better institutions, more abundance, less suffering) follows more easily once the information-processing layer improves.
